verdict.rationale: Cua's own Driver exposes MCP and a CLI so agents like Claude Code, Codex and Cursor can drive native apps, which lets users simply "ask the agent to do things in your apps." Spaces can also be followed from your own agent. The natural-language layer itself comes from those external agents rather than a first-party conversational interface. One hands-on report of an older cua-agent build shows it typing in the wrong place and failing to connect, though that is not enough to dispute the current docs. Missing for 10: a first-party natural-language interface for operating Cua itself (creating and managing Spaces), detailed docs on the natural-language workflow, and independent corroboration that natural-language operation works reliably in current versions.
